Industries

Built for the operational realities of industrial manufacturers and distributors.

Lattice & Spire is configured for the categories, regulations, and supplier dynamics specific to each industry we serve. Not a generic platform with an industry label — purpose-built configurations developed with category leaders in each vertical.

· 6 verticals· 340+ enterprises· 41 countries
Automotive

Multi-tier visibility for OEMs, tier-1s, and the dual-source playbook for 2026.

Automotive supply chains run on six-tier dependencies, JIT-tuned inventory, and PPAP-bound supplier qualification. A single tier-2 disruption — a semiconductor fab outage, a rare-earth export control, a tier-3 plant fire — can park a line for weeks.

Lattice & Spire is deployed across OEMs, electric-vehicle programs, and tier-1 system suppliers to map true multi-tier exposure, monitor leadtime drift in real time, and orchestrate dual-source qualification when conditions demand it.

automotive · multi-tier visibility

Where automotive supply chains break

  • Tier-2 semiconductor & sensor exposure with no direct visibility
  • PPAP backlog when tier-1 supplier qualification stretches 22+ weeks
  • Single-source critical components carried across multiple programs
  • Aftermarket parts forecasting that ignores leadtime distributions
  • EV program component risk concentrated in five geographies

How Lattice & Spire helps

  • Network Graph maps tier-2 and tier-3 dependencies using public trade data
  • Risk Radar flags sensor & semi-fab disruption 8–12 weeks ahead of impact
  • Dual-source readiness dashboard ranked by qualification cost and time
  • Contract Vault surfaces PPAP obligations across the program portfolio
Marlowe
Industrial

Marlowe Industrial — a tier-1 system supplier with 18 plants — cut tier-2 semiconductor exposure from $48M to $11M in eighteen months using Lattice & Spire's Network Graph and dual-source playbook.

Aerospace & Defense

For programs where every part is traceable, every supplier is audited, and the wrong miss costs a program slot.

Aerospace and defense procurement operates in a constrained universe of qualified suppliers, NADCAP-certified processes, and ITAR-bound component flows. Tier-1 leadtimes for cast and forged components have expanded from 22 weeks in 2019 to 47 weeks in 2026.

Lattice & Spire is used across commercial airframers, defense primes, and tier-2 specialist suppliers to model program-level material risk, manage qualified-supplier rosters, and operationalize counter-counterfeit traceability.

aerospace · program risk

Where aerospace supply chains break

  • Titanium and superalloy mill capacity allocated against firm program slots
  • Casting and forging leadtimes that have doubled since 2019
  • NADCAP-process backlogs concentrated in 14 specialist suppliers globally
  • Rare-earth materials traceability under shifting export controls
  • Counter-counterfeit obligations under DFARS and AS6174

How Lattice & Spire helps

  • Program-level material exposure mapped to tier-2 and tier-3 inputs
  • Risk Radar tracks 18 signal classes including export controls
  • Qualified-supplier roster management with NADCAP and Nadcap reciprocity
  • Counterfeit detection workflows aligned to AS6174 and AS9120
Westmere
Aero

Westmere Aero, a tier-2 specialist in airframe castings, reduced qualified-supplier identification cycle from 14 weeks to 19 days after deploying Lattice & Spire's Network Graph and Supplier 360.

Download the Aerospace industry brief (PDF, 28pp)
Heavy Equipment

Engineered-to-order programs require contract intelligence and parts visibility on a different time horizon.

Heavy-equipment OEMs build to order, support equipment in the field for 20+ years, and carry parts catalogs that exceed 800,000 active SKUs. The procurement category mix spans precision castings, hydraulic systems, electronic control modules, and aftermarket consumables — each with its own supplier dynamics.

Lattice & Spire is deployed across mining, construction, agricultural, and material-handling OEMs to unify ETO project procurement, aftermarket forecasting, and field-installed-base risk.

heavy equipment · ETO + aftermarket

Where heavy-equipment supply chains break

  • ETO program procurement disconnected from aftermarket parts planning
  • 800,000+ SKU catalogs with stale supplier and lifecycle data
  • Long-tail electronic components facing 60+ week leadtimes
  • Dealer-network parts forecasting that lags equipment installed base
  • Hydraulic and powertrain suppliers concentrated in three regions

How Lattice & Spire helps

  • Unified part master across ETO and aftermarket procurement
  • Forecast Engine blends installed base data with dealer demand signals
  • Long-tail component leadtime monitoring with auto-escalation
  • Network Graph maps powertrain & hydraulics concentration risk
Strathmore
Heavy Ind.

Strathmore Heavy Industries recovered $14.2M annualized savings within twelve months by consolidating supplier data across four ERPs and operationalizing dual-source readiness on critical hydraulic components.

Read the Strathmore case study
Industrial Distribution

For distributors managing 1.4M-SKU catalogs and 5,000-supplier rosters.

Industrial distribution runs on category breadth, supplier rebate structures, and an unrelenting cycle of pricing and availability decisions. Margin compression has accelerated since 2023, and the distributors winning are the ones whose category teams have real-time visibility into supplier health, contract economics, and demand signal shifts.

Lattice & Spire is deployed across MRO, electrical, fluid-power, and safety distributors to operationalize category strategy with the data their merchandising teams actually need.

distribution · category intelligence

Where distribution supply chains break

  • Rebate structures across 200+ suppliers tracked in spreadsheets
  • Stale supplier master with 18% duplicate-record rates
  • Category margin erosion that takes 14 weeks to surface
  • Long-tail SKU availability data updated weekly at best
  • Supplier-led-price-increase cadence that outpaces response

How Lattice & Spire helps

  • Contract Vault tracks rebate tiers and realization in real time
  • Supplier 360 reduces master-record duplication by 90%+
  • Insights Hub surfaces category margin erosion within 48 hours
  • Risk Radar flags supplier financial-health deterioration early
Trent Valley
Engineering

Trent Valley Engineering, a UK-headquartered MRO distributor, recovered £3.8M in unrealized rebates in its first twelve months on Contract Vault — and reduced supplier-master duplication from 22% to under 4%.

Download the Industrial Distribution brief (PDF, 24pp)
Chemicals & Materials

Feedstock economics, regulatory exposure, and the Scope 3 reporting wall.

Chemicals manufacturers operate at the intersection of volatile feedstock pricing, shifting regulatory regimes (REACH, TSCA, CSRD), and customer ESG demands that increasingly cascade upstream. The traditional procurement levers — long-term agreements, forward buys, regional sourcing — are necessary but no longer sufficient.

Lattice & Spire is deployed across specialty chemicals, polymers, and advanced materials companies to operationalize feedstock intelligence, regulatory obligation tracking, and Scope 3 emissions reporting at supplier-line-item granularity.

chemicals · feedstock + regulatory

Where chemicals supply chains break

  • Feedstock pricing exposure modelled monthly, not continuously
  • REACH and TSCA obligation tracking spread across regulatory affairs
  • Scope 3 emissions estimated at category level, not line-item
  • Customer ESG questionnaires consuming weeks of category-team time
  • Supplier sustainability disclosures uneven and uncomparable

How Lattice & Spire helps

  • Continuous feedstock-price monitoring tied to forward purchase coverage
  • Regulatory obligation tracking integrated with supplier master
  • Scope 3 emissions calculated at PO-line granularity with CSRD-ready exports
  • Supplier sustainability questionnaire automation with response benchmarking
Helmstedt
Polymers

Helmstedt Polymers reduced its CSRD-disclosure preparation time from 14 weeks to 19 days by operationalizing Scope 3 calculation at PO-line granularity through Lattice & Spire's ESG Tracker.

Download the Chemicals industry brief (PDF, 26pp)
Food & Beverage Manufacturing

Ingredient traceability, FSMA compliance, and the agricultural commodity layer.

Food and beverage manufacturers operate on the most consequential of supply chains — every ingredient is regulated, every lot is traceable, and every recall is reputational. Layer on agricultural commodity exposure, packaging cost volatility, and increasingly granular consumer-facing sustainability claims, and the data demands escalate quickly.

Lattice & Spire is deployed across CPG, ingredient, and packaging manufacturers to operationalize lot-level traceability, ingredient supplier qualification, and FSMA-aligned recall readiness.

food & bev · traceability

Where food & bev supply chains break

  • Lot-level ingredient traceability spread across plant-level systems
  • FSMA 204 recordkeeping requirements as of 2026
  • Agricultural commodity exposure modelled outside of procurement
  • Packaging supplier disruption affecting six production lines at once
  • Sustainability claim substantiation under FTC and CMA scrutiny

How Lattice & Spire helps

  • Lot-level traceability across plant, supplier, and farm-tier
  • FSMA 204 recordkeeping aligned to the traceability rule
  • Ingredient-supplier risk monitoring including weather signal classes
  • Packaging-supplier concentration mapping across the plant network
Quintana
Foods Global

Quintana Foods Global, a multi-category CPG manufacturer with 23 plants, reduced ingredient-recall containment time from 72 hours to 4 hours through lot-level traceability operationalized in Lattice & Spire.
